title: Replace ordered dyad grouping with deterministic unordered dyad grouping
trigger: Exact-SHA Group-2 identity audit showed source dyad tokens are not stable pair keys and the same social pair can occur in both communication directions.

amendment.derivation: Pseudonymize Initiator_ID and Recipient_ID with a runtime HMAC secret; lexicographically sort the two pseudonyms; hash the ordered tuple with a fixed D0019 dyad namespace. A↔B therefore shares one group.
amendment.source_dyad_column: Preserve as source provenance only; never use as the primary fold grouping key.
amendment.fallback: Initiator_ID pseudonym only if a valid recipient/dyad cannot be constructed under the frozen RDC-004 missingness rules. If neither is valid, HELD_SPLIT.
amendment.event_identity: Canonical Event_ID is deterministic from exact source version/file SHA/sheet/original row. Preserve source `event` and Collection_Year as secondary provenance; do not rely on source `event` alone because it repeats.
amendment.model_change: NONE. B0/B1/B2, C, preprocessing, metrics, Group2 development and Group1 one-time transfer rules are unchanged.

rationale: Grouping is intended to block dependence/leakage across repeated interactions. An ordered A→B key can place A→B and B→A observations from the same social pair in different folds. The source-schema audit was conducted before empirical model fitting or outcome-performance inspection, so this amendment reduces leakage without outcome-driven optimization.
scientific_boundary: This is a validation/provenance correction, not biological evidence and not a claim about signal meaning.
supersedes: RDC-004-F05 note specifying deterministic ordered Initiator_ID→Recipient_ID pair
